contrary_evidence: Global equity resilience and gains in several regional markets argue against a uniform tightening interpretation.
Ringgit, won and Taiwan dollar recovery on 25 September show that emerging-market currency pressure is not generalized.
Hormuz negotiations had not yet produced a verified physical-system change, so oil relief could still reflect a change in probabilities rather than realized throughput.
limitations: Several 25 September market observations are intraday snapshots and can change by the close.

Attribution of equity resilience to AI earnings expectations and prospective Middle East energy relief relies partly on contemporaneous market reporting rather than a fully observed causal decomposition.
The report does not establish broad corporate or sovereign refinancing stress; it treats wider refinancing effects as conditional.
notes: Revision 3 is a build-validation correction after public revision 2. en.title: Global Macro — Risk assets resist the bond selloff as stress concentrates in rates and emerging-market FX
en.deck: Global equities are heading for their best week since early August even as long sovereign yields remain near multi-decade highs, revealing a selective cross-asset shock rather than uniform tightening.
en.regime: Cross-asset divergence: equity risk appetite remains resilient while long sovereign yields and selected emerging-market currencies absorb more of the rate-and-energy shock.
